Can't reproduce this, if I paste the code into a `+layout.ts` and generate the types I get 
```
Type '() => { foo: string; }' is not assignable to type 'LayoutLoad<void | (Partial<PageData> & Record<string, any>)>'.
  Type '{ foo: string; }' is not assignable to type 'MaybePromise<void | (Partial<PageData> & Record<string, any>)>'.
    Type '{ foo: string; }' is not assignable to type 'Partial<PageData> & Record<string, any>'.
      Type '{ foo: string; }' is not assignable to type 'Partial<PageData>'.
        Types of property 'foo' are incompatible.
          Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.ts(2322)
```

@dummdidumm I believe the problem only exists when there's also a `+page.ts`, I'm not quite sure though, this is peculiarly difficult to reproduce for some reason.
Anyway, here you go, a repro: https://github.com/aradalvand/sveltekit-load-typing-problem

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26527405/187076883-270b254b-da19-45eb-bfd0-483854210a93.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26527405/187076892-2f3bb006-c61d-4dc2-84b1-d928a97eb3a2.png)
Still can't reproduce it, I get the expected error in `+layout.ts`

Wow, that's pretty weird... 🤔
I don't know, maybe you can close this issue and wait to see if this is reported again, if not, then it's probably a glitch on my side. Thanks.
Does that mean it's consistently reproducible on your end with your repo, or can't you reproduce it either reliably?

I can reproduce it like 50% of the time, which is weird.
Sometimes it works as expected and there's an error, sometimes there isn't — for what it's worth, in my actual project I couldn't get it to produce an error no matter how many times I cleared the `.svelte-kit` directory or restarted the TS server, but in the repro I linked above, it fluctuates, sometimes the error appears. Strange.
@aradalvand I think the problem happens if the load function is async. Can you confirm?

I think I understand the problem better now.
1. Right now the logic is "if there's a page(.server) file, assume that it has a load function". This isn't always correct. We may need to statically analyze each of those files to see if that's really true - update: fixed through #7050
2. (possible bug uncovered while playing around) when I delete a `+page.js` file next to a `layout.js` file the types don't get updated - update: fixes through #7002 
3. Even with 1 and 2 getting resolved, there's still the "problem" that the type of `LayoutLoad` assumes that it's the `PageLoad`'s job to fill out the required fields. `LayoutLoad` will only get more strict typings if not all children have load functions. I don't see a way to make this work so that it works as wanted here, since this is a cyclic relationship: In order to know what type `LayoutLoad` is, it would need to know what return type `PageLoad` has. To know what type `PageLoad` to restrict to, it needs to know the return type of `LayoutLoad` (properties already set in `LayoutLoad` are no longer required in `PageLoad`).

Since 1 and 2 are resolved and 3 can't be changed / is "works as designed", I'm closing this.
